ADMINISTRATION AND CONTROL  0.1 Administration and Control 0.1.1 Statement  (A) Turkish Airlines hereby certifies that the Operations Manual Part-A has been established in compliance with Turkish DGCA/EASA and all applicable regulations and with the terms and the conditions of the Turkish Airlines Air Operator Certificate (AOC). (B) This Operations Manual contains operational instructions that are to be complied with by the relevant personnel. (C) This Operations Manual including amendments and/or revisions shall be submitted to authority for acceptance and approval prior to being enforced. (D) The undersigned declare that they know and understand the content of this manual and they will perform their duties in full accordance with this manual.  0.2 General 0.2.1 Copyright  Copying of whole or any parts of Turkish Airlines Operations Manual Part-A whether as electronic or paper copies by third parties without prior written authorization by Turkish Airlines is prohibited (for detailed information, see   PL.10.85.001 Information Security  Policy).  0.2.2 Introduction  (A) The restrictions specified within this manual are Turkish Airlines’ standards. In case of natural disaster, humanitarian flight and national security reasons an exemption may be made by the approval of Chief Flight Operations Officer. On the other hand, if the specified restriction is because of Turkish DGCA requirement, an exemption may be made by the approval of the Authority for the same reasons. (B) The Turkish Airlines’ Operations Manual (OM) consists of separate parts/volumes: 1.   EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A: which is explained in this volume comprises the “General/Basic” part. It contains the operational policies, instructions and procedures required for a safe operation. It explains the duties and responsibilities of all ground and flight operations personnel and their interrelationship to the operations as a whole in detail.   EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A is issued in accordance with the Turkish DGCA Requirements. It complies with Turkish DGCA/EASA regulations and with the terms and conditions of the Turkish Airlines AOC (Air Operator Certificate). 2.   Operations Manual Part-B: is designed and developed in accordance with the guidelines of safe operating policies, procedures and techniques as published by manufacturers or authorities for all aeroplane types currently operated by Turkish Airlines. a. 0.2.7 System of Amendment  (A) The Flight Operations Coordination Manager is responsible for updating, editing and publishing the hard and soft copies of  EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A on behalf of the Chief Flight Operations Officer (Nominated Person for Flight Operations). (B)   EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A will be amended by the Flight Operations Coordination Management whenever deemed necessary to reflect changes in rules, regulations, standards, policies, procedures, operational conditions and requirements etc. for the safe conduct of all Turkish Airlines operations. (C) When immediate amendments or revisions are required in the interest of safety, they may be published and applied immediately according to   TL.18.006 Instruction On Document Preparation, Review and Approval Operations Section 6.3.1.2 Approval/Acceptance Process for Documents to be approved by Authority, provided that any approval required has been granted. Turkish Airlines shall incorporate all amendments and revisions required by the Turkish DGCA and ensure that information taken from approved documents, and any amendment thereof, is correctly reflected in the operations manual. This does not prevent Turkish Airlines from publishing more conservative data and procedures in the operations manual. (D) The hard copy amendment will only be provided to the related departments via co-mail by the Flight Operations Directorate. (E) The amendment will also be provided to all Turkish Airlines employees via the DDMS and/or the mobile applications for crew. (F) The revision process for the reserved copies of   EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A for each Turkish Airlines aeroplanes will be handled by the Flight Operations Coordination Management and will be forwarded to the Navigational Documentation Supervisor’s Office to replace the obsolete ones. (G) The revised text on an amendment page will be indicated by a vertical line in the left-hand margin (for details, see TL.18.006  Instruction On Document Preparation, Review and Approval Operations Section 6.1.3.2 Procedure and Instruction Sections). (H) The header of each page within this manual contains Turkish Airlines Logo, manual name, chapter name, document number, revision number. The footer of each page contains page number. (I) The document name, number, approval dates, revision number and date, date of entry into force, and the names and electronic signatures of the persons who are the owner(s), reviewer, approver(s), and in charge of the document will be as published in DDMS cover page. (J) No handwritten amendments or revisions shall be made within this manual unless otherwise instructed by the Flight Operations Directorate for the interest of safety.  0.2.8 Holder’s Responsibility  (A) Any holder receiving an amendment either in hard or soft copy format shall study the revised temporary revision texts upon receipt not later than the effective date. (B) Any holder receiving a hard copy amendment shall insert the temporary revisions at the first opportunity. (C) Previous amendment letters and obsolete pages shall be removed and destroyed. (D)   EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A provided by the Flight Operations Directorate in electronic format is read only and contains whole amended manual. (E) Any discrepancy, error or difficulty shall be reported to the Flight Operations Coordination Management.  0.2.9. === Sayfa 22 ===
Advanced Aircraft  An aircraft with equipment in addition to that required for a basic aircraft for a given take-off, approach or landing operation.  Aerodrome Operating Minima  “Aerodrome operating minima” means the limits of usability of an aerodrome for: take-off, expressed in terms of runway visual range (RVR) and/or visibility and, if necessary, ceiling; landing in 2D instrument approach operations, expressed in terms of visibility and/or RVR, minimum descent altitude/height (MDA/H) and, if necessary, ceiling; landing in 3D instrument approach operations, expressed in terms of visibility and/or  Aeroplane  An engine-driven fixed-wing aircraft heavier than air that is supported in flight by the dynamic reaction of the air against its wings.  Aeroplane Flight Manual / Flight Manual  A manual associated with the certificate of airworthiness that contains information (limits, procedures, data, etc.) required to operate the aeroplane at the level of safety established by the aeroplane's certification basis.  Aircraft  Any machine that can derive support in the atmosphere from the reactions of the air other than the reactions of the air against the earth's surface, it includes aeroplanes and helicopters.  Aircraft Variant  As used with respect to the licensing and operation of flight crew, means an aircraft of the same basic certificated type which contain modifications not resulting in significant changes of handling and / or flight characteristic, or flight crew complement, but causing significant changes to equipment and/or procedures.  Air Operator Certificate (AOC)  A certificate authorizing an operator to carry out specified commercial air transport operations.  Alternate Aerodrome  An adequate aerodrome to which an aircraft may proceed when it becomes either impossible or inadvisable to proceed to or to land at the aerodrome of intended landing where the necessary services and facilities are available, where aircraft performance requirements can be met and which is operational at the expected time of use. Alternate aerodromes include the following:  Take-off alternate   - An alternate aerodrome at which an aircraft can land should it become necessary shortly after take-off and it is not possible to use the aerodrome of departure.  En-route alternate   - An aerodrome at which an aircraft would be able to land after experiencing an abnormal or emergency condition during en-route phase of the flight.  Fuel/Energy Enroute alternate   – (fuel/energy ERA) aerodrome means an ERA Aerodrome that is required at the planning stage for use in the calculation of fuel/energy  Destination alternate   - An alternate aerodrome to which an aircraft may proceed should it become impossible or inadvisable to land at the aerodrome of intended landing. Note: Note The Aerodrome from which a flight departs may also be an en-route or a destination alternate aerodrome for that flight.  Altimetry System Error  The difference between the altitude indicated by the altimeter display, assuming a correct altimeter barometric setting, and the pressure altitude corresponding to the undisturbed ambient pressure. Augmented Flight Crew  A flight crew which comprises more than the minimum number required to operate the aircraft, allowing each flight crew member to leave the assigned post, for the purpose of in-flight rest, and to be replaced by another appropriately qualified flight crew member.  Authority  The competent body responsible for the safety regulation of civil aviation in the State of the applicant or operator. Cabin Crew Member  “Cabin crew member” means an appropriately qualified crew member, other than a flight crew or technical crew member, who is assigned by an operator to perform duties related to the safety of passengers and flight during operations.  CDRM (Cabin Defect Reporting Manual)  A booklet used to explain cabin defects expressed as abbreviated codes that occur in Corporate’s fleet.  Ceiling  The height above the ground or water of the base of the lowest layer of cloud below 6000 m (20000 ft) covering more than half of the sky.  Circling  The visual phase of a circling approach operations  Circling Approach Operation  Circling approach operation means a Type A instrument approach operation to bring an aircraft into position for landing on a runway/final approach and take-off area (FATO) that is not suitably located for a straight-in approach;  Commander  Pilot designated by Turkish Airlines or by the designated commander as being in command and charged with the safe conduct of the flight for the purpose of commercial air transport operations.  Commercial Operation  “Commercial operation” means any operation of an aircraft, in return for remuneration or other valuable consideration, which is available for the public or, when not made available to the public, which is performed under a contract between an operator and a customer, where the latter has no control over the operator.  Contaminated Runway  A runway is contaminated when more than 25 % of one third of the runway surface area (whether in isolated areas or not) within the required length and width being used is covered by one or more of the following substances: Compacted snow, Dry snow more than 3 mm deep, Heavy frost, Ice, Slush more than 3 mm deep, Standing water more than 3 mm deep, Wet ice, and Wet snow more than 3 mm deep. === Sayfa 24 ===
Runway Surface Condition Descriptors: Compacted Snow:   Snow that has been compacted into a solid mass such that aeroplane tires, at operating pressures and loadings, will run on the surface without significant further compaction or rutting of the surface.  Dry snow:   Snow from which a snowball cannot readily be made.  Frost:   Frost consists of ice crystals formed from airborne moisture on a surface whose temperature is at or below freezing. Frost differs from ice in that the frost crystals grow independently and therefore have a more granular texture. Note: Note  Note 1 : Below freezing refers to air temperature equal to or less than the freezing point of water (0 Degree Celcisus).  Note: Note  Note 2 : Under certain conditions frost can cause the surface to become very slippery and it is then reported appropriately as reduced braking action.  Ice:   Water that has frozen or compacted snow that has transitioned into ice, in cold and dry conditions.  Slush:   Snow that is so water-saturated that water will drain from it when a handful is picked up or will splatter if stepped on forcefully.  Standing Water:   Water of depth greater than 3 mm.  Wet ice:   Ice with water on top of it or ice that is melting.  Wet Snow:   Snow that contains enough water content to be able to make a well-compacted, solid snowball, but water will not squeeze out.  Continuous Descent Final Approach (CDFA)  “Continuous descent final approach (CDFA)” means a technique, consistent with stabilized approach procedures, for flying the final approach segment (FAS) of an instrument non-precision approach (NPA) procedure as a continuous descent, without level-off, from an altitude/height at or above the final approach fix altitude/height: 1. for straight-in approach operations, to a point approximately 15 m (50 ft) above the landing runway threshold or the point where the flare maneuver begins; or 2. for circling approach operations, until MDA/H or visual flight maneuver altitude/height is reached;  Co-pilot  A pilot serving in any piloting capacity other than as pilot-in-command or Commander, but excluding a pilot who is on board the aircraft for the sole purpose of receiving flight instruction for a license or rating.  Crew Member  A person assigned by Turkish Airlines to perform duties on an aircraft.  Crew Concept  The pre-flight check during which the activities assuring that no maintenance operation is needed, and that the aircraft is appropriate for the scheduled flight are carried out under the pilot's responsibility.  Critical Phases of Flight  “Critical phases of flight” in the case of aeroplanes means the take-off run, the take-off flight path, the final approach, the missed approach, the landing, including the landing roll, and any other phases of flight as determined by the Commander.  Cruise Pilot  “Cruise Pilot” means a pilot who relieves the Commander of his duties at the controls during the cruise phase of a flight in multipilot operations above FL200. === Sayfa 25 ===
Articles or substances which are capable of posing significant risk to health, safety or property when transported by air and which are classified according to   DK.31.006 ICAO Doc 9284 | Technical Instructions For The Safe Transport Of Dangerous Goods By Air.  Decision Altitude / Decision Height  “Decision altitude (DA) or decision height (DH)” means a specified altitude or height in a 3D instrument approach operation at which a missed approach procedure must be initiated if the required visual reference to continue the approach has not been established.  Designated Commander  The commander designated by Turkish Airlines to be in command of the aircraft for the assigned leg(s).  Directorate General of Civil Aviation (Turkish DGCA)  The competent directorate responsible for the safety regulation of civil aviation in Türkiye (SHGM-Sivil Havacılık Genel Müdürlüğü).  Dry Runway  A dry runway is one which is neither wet nor contaminated, and includes those paved runways which have been specially prepared with grooves or porous pavement and maintained to retain effectively good braking action even when moisture is present.  Electronic Flight Bag (EFB)  The cockpit system, which enables for the performance of the flight operation through the electronic documentation and calculation software by means of the least documentation, as much as possible, at the flight deck within the scope of the Paperless Cockpit project.  Exemption  A formal authorization issued by the Turkish DGCA providing relief from part or all of the provisions of a Turkish DGCA regulation(s). The authorization may or may not be conditional.  Final Approach Segment  “Final approach segment (FAS)” means that segment of an instrument approach procedure (IAP) in which alignment and descent for landing are accomplished;  Flight Crew Member  “Flight crew member” means a licensed crew member charged with duties essential to the operation of an aircraft during a flight duty period;  Flight Deck  The area of an aircraft designed to enable the pilot(s) to operate the aircraft, which contains the required instrumentation, controls, systems and equipment, and is separated from other areas of the aircraft. “Flight Crew Compartment” or “Cockpit” may be used as equivalent terms.  Flight Monitoring  “Flight monitoring” means, in addition to the requirements defined for flight following: 1. operational monitoring of flights by suitably qualified operational-control personnel from departure throughout all phases of the flight; 2. communication of all available and relevant safety information between the operational-control personnel on the ground and the flight crew; and 3. critical assistance to the flight crew in the event of an in-flight emergency or security issue, or at the request of the flight crew.  Flight Time  The total time from the moment an aeroplane first moves for the purpose of taking off until the moment it finally comes to rest at the end of the flight.  Go-around  “Go-around” means a transition from an approach operation to a stabilized climb. This includes maneuvers conducted at or above the MDA/H or DA/H, or below the DA/H (balked landings);  Head-Up Display Landing System (HUDLS) E K . 1 0 . 7 3 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 6 O p e r a t i o n s M a n u a l P a r t - A QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 23 | Total Page: 466 Copy of this document has been generated on 9.01.2026 21:53. === Sayfa 26 ===
“Head-up display landing system (HUDLS)” means the total airborne system which provides head-up guidance to the pilot to enable the pilot to either control the aircraft or to monitor the autopilot during take-off (if applicable), approach and landing (and roll-out if applicable), or go-around. It includes all the sensors, computers, power supplies, indications and controls.  Installed EFB  An EFB host platform installed in the aircraft and considered as an aircraft part, covered, thus, by the aircraft airworthiness approval.  Landing Distance Available (LDA)  The length of the runway which is declared available by the appropriate Authority and suitable for the ground run of an aeroplane landing.  Line Check  “Line check” means a check conducted by the operator and completed by the pilot or the technical crew member to demonstrate competence in carrying out normal line operations described in   EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A.  Low Visibility Operations (LVO)  “Low visibility operations (LVO)” means approach or take-off operations on a runway with a runway visual range less than 550 m or a decision height less than 200 ft.  Low Visibility Procedures (LVP)  “Low visibility procedures” means procedures applied at an aerodrome for the purpose of ensuring safety during low-visibility operations.  Master Minimum Equipment List (MMEL)  A list established for a particular aircraft type by the manufacturer with the approval of the State of Manufacture containing items, one or more of which is permitted to be unserviceable at the commencement of a flight. The MMEL may be associated with special operating conditions, limitations or procedures.  Minimum descent altitude (MDA) or Minimum descent height (MDH)  MDA or MDH means a specified altitude or height in a 2D instrument approach operation or circling approach operation below which descent must not be made without the required visual reference.  Minimum Equipment List (MEL)  A list which provides for the operation of aeroplane, subject to specified conditions, with particular equipment inoperative, prepared by the operator in conformity with, or more restrictive than, the MMEL established for the aeroplane type.  Night  The hours between the end of evening civil twilight and the beginning of morning civil twilight or such other period between sunset and sunrise, as may be prescribed by the appropriate authority.  Operational Control  The exercise of authority over the initiation, continuation, diversion or termination of a flight in the interest of the safety of the flight.  Operational Credit  A credit authorized for operations with an advanced aircraft enabling a lower aerodrome operating minimum than would normally be authorized for a basic aircraft, based upon the performance of advanced aircraft systems utilizing the available external infrastructure.  Performance Based Aerodrome Operating Minima (PBAOM)  A lower aerodrome operating minimum, for a given take-off, approach or landing operation, than is available when using a basic aircraft. PBAOM may be based on Operational Credit and are not limited to PBN operations.  Pilot Flying (PF)  A pilot who, for the time being, is in charge of the controls of an aircraft. === Sayfa 27 ===
A pilot who is assisting the Pilot Flying in accordance with the multi-crew co-operation concept, when the required flight crew is more than one.  Pilot-in-Command (PIC)  Pilot designated as being in command and charged with the safe conduct of the flight. For the purpose of commercial air transport, the “pilot-in-command” shall be termed “commander”.  Portable EFB  Portable EFB is not part of the aircraft configuration and are considered to be PEDs. They generally have self-contained power and may rely on data connectivity to achieve full functionality. Modifications to the aircraft to use portable EFBs require the appropriate airworthiness approval depending on the State’s regulatory framework.  Portable Electronic Devices (PED)  PEDs are any kind of electronic device, typically but not limited to consumer electronics, brought on board the aircraft by crew members, passengers, or as part of the cargo and that are not included in the approved aircraft configuration. All equipment that is able to consume electrical energy falls under this definition. The electrical energy can be provided from internal sources as batteries (chargeable or non-rechargeable) or the devices may also be connected to specific aircraft power sources.  Precision Approach  An instrument approach using Instrument Landing System, Microwave Landing System or Precision Approach Radar for guidance in both azimuth and elevation.  Psychoactive Substances  Psychoactive   substances   are:   alcohol,   opioids,   cannabinoids,   sedatives   and   hypnotics,   other   psychostimulants,   cocaine,   other stimulants, hallucinogens and volatile solvents.  Safe Landing  “Safe landing” means, in the context of the fuel/energy policy or fuel/energy schemes, a landing at an adequate aerodrome or operating site with no less than the final reserve fuel/energy remaining and in compliance with the applicable operational procedures and aerodrome operating minima.  Short Flight Plan (SFP)  Short Flight Plan (SFP) is the first page of the Operational Flight Plan (OFP).  Short Runway  A runway to be used for landing with a LDA or for take-off with a TORA lengths below 6,500 feet (1,982 meters).  Stabilized Approach  Refer to   Subchapter 8.3.2.1.6.  Sterile Cockpit (Sterile Flight Crew Compartment)  “Sterile flight crew compartment” means any period of time when the flight crew members are not disturbed or distracted, except for matters critical to the safe operation of the aircraft or the safety of the occupants.  Take-off Distance Available (TODA)  The length of the take-off run available plus the length of the clearway available.  Take-off Run Available (TORA)  The length of runway which is declared available by the appropriate Authority and suitable for the ground run of an aeroplane taking off.  Target Off-Block Time (TOBT)  The time that an aircraft operator / handling agent estimates that an aircraft will be ready, all doors closed, boarding bridge removed, push back vehicle present, ready to start up / push back immediately upon reception of clearance from the TWR. === Sayfa 28 ===
Type A instrument approach operation means an instrument approach operation with an MDH or a DH at or above 250 ft;  Type B Instrument Approach Operation  Type B instrument approach operation means an operation with a DH below 250 ft. Type B instrument approach operations are categorised as: (a) Category I (CAT I): a DH not lower than 200 ft and with either a visibility not less than 800 m or an RVR not less than 550 m; (b) Category II (CAT II): a DH lower than 200 ft but not lower than 100 ft, and an RVR not less than 300 m; (c) Category III (CAT III): a DH lower than 100 ft or no DH, and an RVR less than 300 m or no RVR limitation;  Total Vertical Error  The vertical geometric difference between the actual pressure altitude flown by an aircraft and its assigned pressure altitude (flight level).  Weather-Permissible Aerodrome  “Weather-permissible aerodrome” means an adequate aerodrome where, for the anticipated time of use, meteorological reports, or forecasts, or any combination thereof, indicate that the meteorological conditions will be at or above the required aerodrome operating minima, and the runway surface condition reports indicate that a safe landing will be possible.  Wet Runway  A runway is considered wet when the runway surface is covered with water or equivalent, less than specified under “Contaminated Runway” above or when there is sufficient moisture on the runway surface to cause it to appear reflective, but without significant areas of standing water.  0.4.2 Abbreviations for EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A  A  AAL: Above Aerodrome Level ABAS: Aircraft Based Augmentation System ACARS: Aircraft Communication Addressing and Reporting System ACAS: Airborne Collision Avoidance System A/C: Aircraft ACC: Area Control Centre ACMS: Aircraft Condition Monitoring System ADI: Attitude Director Indicator ADREP: Accident/Incident Data Reporting System AEA: Association of European Airlines AFM/FM: Aeroplane Flight Manual / Flight Manual AFTN: Aeronautical Fixed Telecommunication Network AFIS: Aerodrome Flight Information Service AGL: Above Ground Level AIP: Aeronautical Information Publication AIRAC: Aeronautical Information Regulation and Control AIS: Aeronautical Information Service AMC: Acceptable Means of Compliance E K . 1 0 . 7 3 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 6 O p e r a t i o n s M a n u a l P a r t - A QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 26 | Total Page: 466 Copy of this document has been generated on 9.01.2026 21:53. ORGANISATION AND RESPONSIBILITIES  1.1 Organisational Structure 1.1.1 General  (A) In order to ensure the safe conduct of air operations, Turkish Airlines maintains a sound and effective management structure that consists of a nominated accountable manager, nominated persons and assigned nominated persons. (B) Turkish Airlines Nominated Accountable Manager (approved by the Turkish DGCA) has corporate authority for ensuring that all operations and maintenance activities are financed and carried out to the standards required by the Turkish DGCA. (C) Turkish Airlines nominated persons (approved by the Turkish DGCA) are responsible for the management and supervision of the following areas: Flight Operations, Ground Operations, Continuing Airworthiness, Crew Training and Security. Detailed information may be found in   PR.10.18.017 Procedure for Authorization Management of Managerial Personnel Requiring Authority Approval. (D) Each individual nominated as a nominated person by Turkish Airlines shall have the qualifications and experience in compliance with set Turkish DGCA requirements. (E)   Nominated   persons   shall   possess   managerial   competency,   technical   and   operational   qualifications,   appropriate   practicable experience, expertise, licensing requirements (as applicable) to ensure the application of aviation safety and security standards and safe operating practices. (B) Commander is accountable to the Chief Flight Operations Officer (Nominated Person for Flight Operations) for the safe, timely and efficient execution of his duties and responsibilities. (C) Commander is responsible for the safety of all crew members, passenger and cargo on board, as soon as he arrives on board the aeroplane, until he leaves the aeroplane at the end of the flight. Safety criteria have authority over all other requirements, therefore, if the Commander determines any ground operations as endangering the safety of the mentioned above, he has final authority on the decision making. (D) Commander is responsible for the safety and operation of the aeroplane from the moment the aeroplane is first ready to move for the purpose of taxiing prior to take-off, until the moment it finally comes to rest at the end of the flight and the engine(s) used as primary propulsion unit(s) is (are) shut down. (E) Commander has final authority over the aeroplane during the time in which he is in command (refer to items (C) and (D) for Commander responsibilities during ground operations). (F) For the purposes of ICAO   DK.21.301 Tokyo Convention On Offences And Certain Other Acts Committed On Board Aircraft an aircraft is considered to be in flight at any time from the moment when all its external doors are closed following embarkation until the moment when any such door is opened for disembarkation; in the case of a forced landing, the flight shall be deemed to continue until the competent authorities take over the responsibility for the aircraft and for persons and property on board (G) Powers of The Aircraft Commander based on ICAO   DK.21.301 Tokyo Convention On Offences And Certain Other Acts Committed On Board Aircraft: 1. The provisions of item (G) shall not apply to offences and acts committed or about to be committed by a person on board an aircraft in flight in the airspace of the State of registration or over the high seas or any other area outside the territory of any State unless the last point of take-off or the next point of intended landing is situated in a State other than that of registration, or the aircraft subsequently flies in the airspace of a State other than that of registration with such person still on board. 2. The aircraft commander may, when he has reasonable grounds to believe that a person has committed, or is about to commit, on board the aircraft, an offence or act contemplated as; offences against penal law, acts which, whether or not they are offences, may or do jeopardize the safety of the aircraft or of persons or property therein or which jeopardize good order and discipline on board, impose upon such person reasonable measures including restraint which are necessary: a. to protect the safety of the aircraft, or of persons or property therein; or b. to maintain good order and discipline on board; or c. to enable him to deliver such person to competent authorities or to disembark him in accordance with the provisions of this item (G). 3. The aircraft commander may require or authorize the assistance of other crew members and may request or authorize, but not require, the assistance of in-flight security officers or passengers to restrain any person whom he is entitled to restrain. Any crew member or passenger may also take reasonable preventive measures without such authorization when he has reasonable grounds to believe that such action is immediately necessary to protect the safety of the aircraft, or of persons or property therein. 4. Measures of restraint imposed upon a person in accordance with item (G), (2) and (3) shall not be continued beyond any point at which the aircraft lands unless: a. such point is in the territory of a non-Contracting State and its authorities refuse to permit disembarkation of that person or those measures have been imposed in accordance with item (B), paragraph (c), in order to enable his delivery to competent authorities; b. the aircraft makes a forced landing and the aircraft commander is unable to deliver that person to competent authorities; or c. that person agrees to onward carriage under restraint. 5. The aircraft commander shall as soon as practicable, and if possible before landing in the territory of a State with a person on board who has been placed under restraint in accordance with the provisions of item (G), (2) and (3), notify the authorities of such State of the fact that a person on board is under restraint and of the reasons for such restraint. 6. The aircraft commander may, in so far as it is necessary for the purpose of offences against penal law, acts which, whether or not they are offences, may or do jeopardize the safety of the aircraft or of persons or property therein or which jeopardize good order and discipline on board, disembark in the territory of any State in which the aircraft lands any person who he has reasonable grounds to believe has committed, or is about to commit, on board the aircraft an act contemplated as acts which, whether or not they are offences, may or do jeopardize the safety of the aircraft or of persons or property therein or which jeopardize good order and discipline on board. 7. The aircraft commander shall report to the authorities of the State in which he disembarks any person pursuant to this item, the fact of, and the reasons for, such disembarkation. 8. The aircraft commander may deliver to the competent authorities of any Contracting State in the territory of which the aircraft lands any person who he has reasonable grounds to believe has committed on board the aircraft an act which, in his opinion, is a serious offence. 9. The aircraft commander shall as soon as practicable and if possible before landing in the territory of a Contracting State with a person on board whom the aircraft commander intends to deliver in accordance with the preceding paragraph, notify the authorities of such State of his intention to deliver such person and the reasons therefor. 10. The aircraft commander shall furnish the authorities to whom any suspected offender is delivered in accordance with the provisions of this item (G), (8), (9) and (10) with evidence and information which are lawfully in his possession. 11. For actions taken in accordance with ICAO   DK.21.301 Tokyo Convention On Offences And Certain Other Acts Committed On Board Aircraft, neither the aircraft commander, any other member of the crew, any passenger, any in-flight security officer, the owner or E K . 1 0 . 7 3 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 6 O p e r a t i o n s M a n u a l P a r t - A QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 63 | Total Page: 466 Copy of this document has been generated on 9.01.2026 21:53. (H) Delegation of duties to other crew members in accordance with procedures laid down in the applicable Operations Manuals shall in no way affect his ultimate responsibility for the safe conduct of the flight. Shall conduct a pre-flight crew briefing (inclusive of the loadmaster, if applicable). Briefing shall be inclusive of the basis for an effective   working   relationship   between   the   flight   crew   and   other   crew   members   with   specific   emphasis   on   Crew   Resource Management (CRM). Items covered during this briefing shall be inclusive of the following minimum items: a. (a) Establish effective communication between the flight crew and other crew members. Specific emphasis shall be made on the guidelines for the use of the Public Address (PA) and interphone systems. b. Guidelines for the use of the flight deck door. c. Discuss items that may be of concern during flight, such as turbulence, smoking. d. Brief the crew as to the current security status of the flight and how security incidents are to be handled. e. Discuss items of routine interest, such as flight time, altitude, route of the flight, and any other specific items relating to the safety requirements for the flight concerned. 35. Shall conduct a post-flight de-briefing of the crew members if he deems necessary. (P) When deemed necessary or as required, the Commander may delegate specific parts of his duties to other crew members with the knowledge that he remains fully responsible for all delegated duties. (Q) For EFB installed aircraft, Commander shall ensure that Jeppesen Flite Deck Pro and all documents in EFB are loaded. (R) Shall fulfill the requirements stated in item   0.2.2 (F). (S) Shall comply with all flight and duty time limitations and rest requirements applicable to their activities. For flight and duty time limitations and rest requirements refer to   Chapter 7. (T) Shall not perform duties on aircraft; 1. when under the influence of psychoactive substances or alcohol or when unfit due to injury, fatigue, medication, sickness or other similar causes; 2. until a reasonable time period has elapsed after deep water diving or following blood donation; 3. if applicable medical requirements not fulfilled; 4. if he is in any doubt of being able to accomplish his assigned duties; or 5. if he knows or suspects that he is suffering from fatigue as referred to in Subchapter 6.1.19, or feels otherwise unfit, to the extent that the flight may be endangered. (U) If he knows or suspects that he is suffering from fatigue, he must not allow their task achievement/decision making to deteriorate to the extent that flight safety is endangered because of the effects of fatigue, taking into account, inter alia, fatigue accumulation, sleep deprivation, number of sectors flown, night duties or time zone changes. Rest periods must provide sufficient time to enable crewmembers to overcome the effects of the previous duties and to be well rested by the start of the following flight duty period. (V) Is responsible for Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) of crew members on board an aircraft according to Occupational Health and Safety Law (No:6331) of Turkish Republic. (W) The commander shall, as soon as possible, report to the appropriate air traffic services (ATS) unit any hazardous weather or flight conditions encountered that are likely to affect flight safety.  1.5 Duties and Responsibilities of Crew Members Other than the Commander 1.5.1 General  (A) A crew member shall be responsible for the proper execution of his duties which are: 1. Related to the safety of the aeroplane and its occupants; and 2. Specified in the instructions and procedures laid down in the Operations Manual. 1.5.2 Co–Pilot  (A) Co-pilot is the deputy of the Commander. (B) Co-pilot is responsible to the Commander to assist in the safe and efficient conduct of the flight. In the event of the incapacitation of the Commander, the Co-pilot shall assume command of the aeroplane. (C) It is the responsibility of the Co-pilot: 1. To observe the provisions of the applicable Operations Manuals in general, and as necessary to fulfil his function and responsibilities as a Co-pilot. 2. To carry out his duties in accordance with the Standard Operating Procedures, including procedures, limitations and performance relating to the specific aeroplane type, as allocated to him by the Commander. 3. To observe the Standard Operating Procedures and inform the Commander of any deviation from the Standard Operating Procedures. 4. To carry out take-offs and landings under the supervision of the Commander. He shall carry out other duties delegated by the Commander in preparation for the flight or during the flight. 5. To confirm the safe navigation of the aeroplane, maintaining a continuous and independent check upon both the geographical position of the aeroplane and its safe terrain clearance. 6. To safely and properly conduct the flight in compliance with the current Operational Flight Plan (OFP) and the Commander’s instructions when the Commander is not at the controls. Any changes to the current OFP shall be notified to the Commander. 7. To vigorously monitor the critical phases of flight, specifically take-off, approach and landing. He shall inform the Commander if there are any deviations from safe standards of operation. 8. To inform and assist the Commander, to ensure the safe and efficient conduct of the flight.Notwithstanding the overriding authority of the Commander, the Co-pilot shall not hesitate to suggest a better course of action if he is convinced that a decision of the Commander merits discussion. The Co-Pilot shall not hesitate to take control of the aircraft (if applicable, initiate a go-around, etc.) if he is convinced that the Commander’s actions endanger flight safety or is convinced the Commander’s status can be classified as incapacitated. 9. To seek and receive such information and/or explanation from the Commander, as may be necessary to enable the Co-pilot to fulfill his duties. 10. To fulfill the requirements stated in item   0.2.2 (F). 11. To submit air safety reports when necessary (Refer to   Chapter 11 Occurrences Subject to Mandatory Reporting).  1.5.3 Cabin Chief  (A) Cabin Chief has overall responsibility to the Commander for the conduct, coordination and performance of cabin operations and safety requirements. (B) Cabin Chief shall be nominated for each commercial passenger flight. (C) Cabin Chief shall verify that all cabin crew members are fit for the duty and that they have the proper documents for the applicable flight. (D) Cabin Chief shall coordinate and organize the functions and tasks of all cabin crew members (cabin crew briefing, delegate positions and working areas, in flight service duties). (E) It is the responsibility of the Cabin Chief: 1. To observe the provisions of the applicable Operations Manuals in general, and as necessary to fulfil his function and responsibilities as Cabin Chief. 2. To ensure proper execution of applicable pre-flight and post-flight security checklists. 3. To verify emergency equipment required for the flight are available. 4. To report matters concerning safety (irregularities and malfunctions) to the Commander. 5. To conduct passenger safety briefings. He shall cross-check and verify critical actions (i.e. checklist items) especially in non-normal situations. (B) He shall be present during self-dispatch, cabin crew, take-off and approach briefings as well as during the review of the AML and MEL/CDL for determining the airworthiness status of the aeroplane. During the jump seat/ observer briefing, the Commander shall ensure that he is properly briefed on safety, security, communication and evacuation procedures. Duties and Responsibilities of Dispatcher  (A) Dispatcher is responsible for providing the Commander with the required data and documents necessary to safely conduct the flight. He shall perform the duties of flight monitoring and if required report to the IOCC and FOCC Manager of any irregularities. He shall coordinate with the maintenance department confirming the airworthiness status of the aeroplane to be dispatched. (B) Dispatcher shall bring to the attention of the IOCC and FOCC Manager any issue/subject with which he disagrees with or causes him concern in reference to flight safety prior to dispatching the flight. If unable to resolve the issue/subject, the Commander shall be informed of the matter and if required to assist in the resolving of the issue (system of shared responsibility). (C) It is the responsibility of the Dispatcher: 1. To observe the provisions of the applicable Operations Manuals in general, and as necessary to fulfil his function and responsibilities as a Dispatcher. 2. To prepare briefing package and support flight crew for handling self-briefing whenever needed, in accordance with the set Turkish Airlines standard requirements. 3. To prepare the Operational Flight Plan and file the Air Traffic Services Flight Plan with the appropriate Authority. 4. To   prepare   the   trip   folder   (OFP,   all   applicable   weather   information,   NOTAMs,   and   route   meteorological   charts   and   related information) in accordance with the set Turkish Airlines standard requirements. 5. To confirm the total amount of fuel required for the flight in accordance with   Subchapter 8.1.7 requirements. 6. To provide information about performance restrictions due to aeroplanes technical status or aerodrome facilities/NOTAMs. 7. To provide information about the availability and technical status of the aeroplane during the dispatch briefing. 8. To report to the Commander any conditions which he believes may affect the safe conduct of the flight. 9. To volunteer such advice, information and assistance to the Commander, as may contribute favorable towards the safe and efficient conduct of the flight. 10. To provide any additional information deemed necessary by the Commander for the safe conduct of a flight. 11. To initiate relevant procedures in the event of an emergency. (D) For detailed job description, see Turkish Airlines   job descriptions.  1.7 Acceptance of Flight Duties Other than Turkish Airlines  Turkish Airlines’ Flight Crew Members are not allowed to fly for or to accept flight duties other than Turkish Airlines’ unless they are authorized by the Authority and/or Turkish Airlines. 2.1.1 Operational Criteria  A) All flights shall be planned and operated in accordance with: 1. Turkish Airlines Regulations and Directives, and 2. Turkish Airlines   EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A,   Operations Manual Part-B,   EK.10.73.002 Operations Manual Part-C and  EK.10.72.001 Operations Manual Part-D, and 3. other Turkish Airlines approved/ published/ distributed relevant documents and manuals. (B) When the documentation listed in item (A) above are contradictory to rules and regulations established and mandated by State Authorities, the more restrictive shall be applicable until revisions can be implemented in the appropriate documentation. (C) In reference to documentation listed in item (A) above, any discrepancies noted shall be reported to the Flight Operations Directorate/Flight Operations Coordination Management. (D) All flights shall be planned and conducted in the following order: 1. Primary factor – SAFETY, then 2. Secondary factors – economical criteria, passenger comfort and operational schedule.  2.1.2. Control and Supervision of Operations  (A) The ultimate responsibility of decision-making for the supervision and control of flight operations activities is held by the Chief Flight Operations Officer. Authority for day-to-day supervision of Turkish Airlines flight operations is delegated by the Chief Flight Operations Officer to the Senior Vice President Integrated Operations Control, IOCC Manager (who then delegates such authority to the on-duty IOCC Duty Managers). While SVP, Integrated Operation Control reports administratively to the Chief Operation Officer, Senior Vice President Integrated Operations Control is responsible to the Chief Flight Operations Officer for the supervision and management activities of the flight operation. (B) In the interest of safety, reliability and efficiency; operational control is the exercise of authority over the initiation, delaying, consolidation, continuation, diversion, termination or cancellation of a flight. (C) In reference to item (A) and (B) above, Chief Flight Operations Officer (Nominated Person) shall: 1. coordinate and supervise the respective flight operations managements; 2. appoint the respective flight operations management personnel; and 3. during his absence, delegate overall supervision of flight operations to the Senior Vice President, Flight Operations. (D) In reference to item (B) above, authority vested in the Commander and the respective flight operations managements for the supervision of flight is delegated to them by the Chief Flight Operations Officer (Nominated Person) based on the system of shared responsibility between the Commander and the respective flight operations managements. (Commander and the respective flight operations managements/dispatchers have joint authority over all preflight decisions. For details refer to   Subchapter 2.3)  2.1.3 License and Qualification Validity  (A) Flight Operations Directorate shall continuously monitor the following: 1. flight crew member qualifications- to be conducted by the applicable Fleet Manager. 2. flight crew member certification- to be conducted by the applicable Fleet Manager. (B) Flight Operations Directorate shall retain up to date qualification, certification and personnel records of flight crew members. (C) Flight Training Directorate shall plan the required Line Flight Under Supervision (LIFUS) and Line Check (LC) for flight crew members. (D) For irregularities regarding the validity of licenses, certificates or qualification, a cross check shall be conducted between the associated crew member and applicable department(s). If required, appropriate training and checking program listed in   Chapter 5 and  EK.10.72.001 Operations Manual Part-D shall be implemented. (E) Each license and certificate holder is responsible for retaining issued licenses and certificates valid. If a flight crew member is in doubt referencing license, certificate or qualification validity, he shall contact the appropriate department for confirmation. License and certificate holders are entitled to exercise issued privileges as long as the license and/or certificate remains valid. Tasks listed below are the specific duties of a flight dispatcher in reference to operational control. Flight dispatcher shall: 1. assist the Commander in the flight preparation by providing the required documents and information; 2. prepare an Operational Flight Plan (OFP) in accordance with Turkish Airlines standards for final approval by the Commander of the flight; 3. prepare an ATS flight plan and file it with the appropriate ATC; 4. obtain the Commanders agreement/approval regarding the filed flight plans; 5. transmit OFP to self-dispatch room for the flight crew (for dispatcher signature requirement, refer to   Subchapter 8.1.10); 6. furnish the Commander with the relevant information prior to and during flight, as necessary, for the safe conduct of the flight; 7. notify the appropriate ATS unit when the position of the aeroplane can not be determined by the aircraft tracking system and attempts to establish communication are unsuccessful; and 8. initiate relevant procedures in the event of an emergency. (B) In performing his duties, it is the responsibility of the flight dispatcher to coordinate with IOCC: 1. on matters of operational planning; and 2. in determining whether or not the flight can be expected to operate routinely within the requirements of   EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A and   EK.10.73.002 Operations Manual Part-C, a. if non-routine operations are expected, OPSC shall coordinate with and support IOCC with alternative plans.  2.3.4 Operational Control Duties and Responsibilities of a Regional Station Manager  Regional station manager shall coordinate with IOCC and take all necessary actions locally. It is continuously monitored and updated with the participation of relevant units if necessary.  2.3.6 Flight Monitoring  (A) The responsibility of flight monitoring is delegated to IOCC. (B) In case of operational irregularities, upon completing the required coordination with the applicable departments and offices, IOCC shall take the necessary actions (operational and/or precautionary). In case of operational irregularities, decision making process shall be based on the following principles: 1. safety factors of flight operations shall never be endangered; 2. passengers, cargo and mail shall reach the final destination with minimum delay; 3. loss of revenue and/or additional expenses shall be kept to a minimum. C) IOCC is responsible for providing the appropriate departments with the necessary information regarding operational irregularity by all acceptable available means.  2.3.8.1 Early Departure of a Flight  (A) For reasons listed in item (B) below, flights may depart prior to the scheduled off-block time with the mutual agreement of the Commander and the station representative. (B) Reasons for early departures: 1. passenger check-in counters have closed for the applicable flight or no additional passengers are expected for the flight (ex. group check-in, flight is full); 2. no additional cargo or mail is expected for the flight; 3. to extend the transit time at the next station provided that no revenue loads are left behind; 4. if the Actual Time of Arrival (ATA) at the next station is expected to be exceeded but nevertheless provided that no revenue loads are left behind; or 5. to avoid certain meteorological or other conditions which may adversely affect the operation of the flight. (C) The following restrictions shall be taken into account when considering an early departure: 1. CTOT, issued slots; 2. operational night restrictions (such as curfew hours, etc.); 3. NOTAMs with operational restrictions (such as, runway or taxiway closures, aerodrome operating hours, etc.); and 4. other relevant limitations. (D) Departure of 11 minutes or greater prior to the scheduled departure time shall only be made with the approval of IOCC. The station representative shall coordinate the issue and inform the Commander accordingly.  2.3.8.2 Delay of a Flight  (A) In case of unforeseen delays, it is the responsibility of all applicable departments, stations and/or crew members to minimize induced delays. (B) Acceptable reasons for delayed flights: 1. to avoid adverse meteorological conditions at the departure aerodrome, en-route or at the aerodrome of destination (this reasoning is under the direct decision of the Commander); 2. passenger boarding (whatever the reasoning); 3. technical defect rectification as indicated in the AML or as deemed necessary by the Commander for the safe conduct of the flight; or 4. to accept Aircraft on Ground (AOG) spare parts for Turkish Airlines grounded aeroplanes. (C) Delays other than item (B) above shall be acceptable to the Commander and IOCC. (D)   All ground delays exceeding or expected to exceed 15 minutes shall be reported to IOCC by the appropriated ground operations personnel. (E)   If flight conditions permit, any delay during approach by ATC (holdings or radar vectors) to Antalya and Istanbul airports should be reported to IOCC. (F) All efforts (safety shall never be compromised) should be taken to reduce the ground time to an absolute minimum for flights operating delayed.  2.3.8.3. No revenue load to or from next station is expected. c. To minimize existing delays. Operational and/or other conditions at the planned destination are prohibiting or render a landing highly improbable (meteorological conditions, runway closure, disaster, strike, etc.). 2. Technical defects detected in flight requiring immediate landing at next suitable aerodrome. 3. Passenger or crew member on board requiring immediate medical assistance. 4. Meteorological conditions encountered or reported en-route requiring alteration of intended routing. 5. Any other reason (unruly passenger, bomb threat, etc.). (B) The authorization to divert while en-route rests entirely with the Commander. The Commander should notify IOCC of his intentions and IOCC should provide recommendations for possible change of route and/or destination or alternate aerodromes. (C) Alternate aerodrome(s) to be selected for diversion (taking into consideration operational and commercial aspects) should be coordinated between the Commander and IOCC. OPSC shall provide flight related information to IOCC in the interest of flight safety.  2.3.8.5. Cancellation of a Flight  (A) Cancellation of a flight means the cancellation of a scheduled or non-scheduled flight or segment of a flight prior to departure (due to lack of equipment, extended delay, meteorological conditions, crew shortage, commercial reasons, etc.). (B) It is Turkish Airlines policy to operate in accordance with the published schedule; certain circumstances (listed below) may however require the cancellation of a flight or segments thereof: 1. By operating a flight with considerable delay, serious difficulties in performing subsequent operations would be created. 2. From a traffic point of view, the conditions are such that a termination of the contract of carriage is feasible or necessary. 3. Additional expenses in operation (ferry flight or utilization of reserve aeroplane etc.) would be far in excess of a possible loss of revenue. 4. Weather conditions at aerodrome of departure and/or destination would cause serious delay on both present and/or subsequent flights. 5. When there is a lack of aeroplanes. (C) The authorization for any flight cancellation rests with IOCC.  2.3.8.6. Consolidation of Flights  (A) Flights may be consolidated either in whole or in segments for the following reasons: 1. Lack of aeroplane(s), 2. Lack of revenue, 3. Other operational reasons. (B) The authorization for flight consolidation rests with IOCC after coordinating with the appropriate departments. 2.4 Powers of Authority 2.4.1 General  (A) Turkish DGCA has the legal obligation to exercise supervisory power over the operations of Turkish Airlines. This authority is stated in Turkish Civil Aviation Laws which is inclusive of the requirements stated in Turkish DGCA/EASA regulations. (B) Turkish Airlines AOC may be varied, suspended or revoked if Turkish DGCA is no longer satisfied that the operations conducted are safe. (C) Turkish DGCA has the privilege to grant an exemption from any requirement prescribed in Turkish DGCA/ EASA regulations. In such case(s), Turkish DGCA is responsible for ensuring that an acceptable level of safety can be maintained. (D) The Accountable Manager, CFOO – Chief Flight Operations Officer; SVP, Technical; SVP, Flight Training; SVP, Ground Operations; SVP, Quality Assurance; SVP, Security and SVP, Corporate Safety shall be acceptable to the Turkish DGCA. Turkish DGCA has the right to interview any nominee or call for additional evidence of his suitability before deciding upon his acceptability. (E) Turkish DGCA has the power to: 1. Determine the adequacy, relevance and consistency of the Turkish Airlines compliance with the requirements. 2. Assess the efficiency of Turkish Airlines internal monitoring procedures and confirm the availability of sufficient resources and proper processes, as documented by Turkish Airlines Quality System. 3. Verify by means of inspections, compliance with the requirements and the effectiveness of the Turkish Airlines Quality System. (F) Turkish DGCA has the authority to assess the continued competence of Turkish Airlines by inspection and monitoring of: 1. Infrastructure, 2. Manuals, 3. Training, 4. Crew records, 5. Continuing Airworthiness, 6. Ramp, 7. Equipment, 8. Pre-flight preparation, 9. Release of Flight/Dispatch, 10. Flight Operations, 11. Ground Operations, 12. Dangerous Goods, 13. Quality System/Compliance Monitoring Program and results of Turkish Airlines Quality audits. Personnel authorized by Turkish DGCA to carry out certification and/ or oversight tasks shall be empowered to perform at least the following tasks: 1. Records, data, procedures, and any other material relevant to the execution of the certification and/ or oversight task; 2. Take copies of or extracts from such records, data, procedures and other material; Ask for an oral explanation on site; 3. Enter relevant premises, operating sites or means of transport; 4. Perform audits, investigations, assessments, inspections, including ramp inspections and unannounced inspections, 5. Take or initiate enforcement measures as appropriate. (G) Authority inspections conducted on the premises of Turkish Airlines, a competent member of the department to be inspected shall accompany the member of the Authority inspecting. 3.3 Handling, Notifying and Reporting of Occurrences  (A) Flight Safety is the number one priority for Turkish Airlines. Reporting of incidents and accidents improves flight safety by correlating the data and identifying potential problem areas. As such, reporting of all incidents and accidents should be considered of utmost importance and flight crew members are encouraged to submit a written report when an occurrence that could potentially have an adverse effect on the safety of flight operations has been observed.   PL.10.21.001 The Safety Policy represents Turkish Airlines’ perspective on Flight Safety. The original document may be reached from DDMS on http://infoportal.thy.com and/or mobile applications for crew. (B) Turkish Airlines is determined and prepared to operate at the highest levels and standards of safety. As is it already well known safety is at the core of an airline’s existence. It is with this that we try to operate safely; conduct our operations and try to please our customers, all in one. As management we would like to reassure our employees that it is our goal to accomplish the former mentioned with the utmost of priority. Having said this, we fully trust and believe that our employees will approach the subject with as much sensitivity and responsibility as possible, and will share any Information that would be beneficial to flight safety. To fulfill this goal, the Corporate Safety Directorate has created a "Confidential/Voluntary Reporting System”. The system helps to improve flight safety through the inputs of the employees. As long as reports are not part of a mandatory submission the submitter or those involved are by no means subject to any penalty or disciplinary action. This exemption will not stand for those incidents and accidents involving third party notifications or any legal ramifications. The information submitted will only be used for enhancing the safety of flight operations within the company. Aside from being the priority of managers, ensuring flight safety should be everyone's priority and duty. As employees, we should do all that we can to be the industry's safest airline.  3.4 Safety Reporting System (SRS)  (A) The SRS system that has been implemented by Turkish Airlines is a comprehensive centralized set of tools that integrates analysis of risk-related activities across the organization including safety and security management. The SRS process includes mandatory reporting, confidential reporting, accident/incident reporting, FDM data, analysis and investigation through to auditing and corrective action tracking. The first step in the system flow is to report an event or a potential occurrence through the web interface or mobile application in the form of an e-report which can be accessed through Turkish Airlines SRS portal ( aqdportal.thy.com). This e-report is processed by a report administrator responsible for each particular type of report and saved as an occurrence within the database. (B) The SRS tool was set up to gather input from any employee via either a compatible web browser or a mobile application, which also allows offline reporting, available to download on internet. Each user, once logged in, will have a variety of reporting options specifically designed for their field of operations. Flight Crew can submit safety related reports but not limited with the following: Air Safety Report (ASR) Confidential Report (CFR) Fatigue Report (FGR) Hazard Report (HAZ)  3.4.1 Mandatory Occurrence Reports (MOR)  A fundamental part of Turkish Airlines Safety Management System is the occurrence reporting process and subsequent investigations and hazard analysis. This calls upon every employee to contribute to safety by reporting any occurrences in order to understand the root cause and to help with the investigation of events to prevent further unforeseen occurences and by learning from these occurrences a more serious or catastrophic situation may be prevented. The Publication DK.22.062 SHT-OLAY Instruction On  Reporting Safety Incidents In Civil Aviation details procedures, with regard to the reportable occurrences, that must be notified to the Turkish DGCA according to national practices. In addition to   DK.22.062 SHT-OLAY Instruction On Reporting Safety Incidents In Civil Aviation, Turkish Airlines Corporate Safety Directorate has initiated a comprehensive Mandatory Occurrence Reporting schemes, in the form of safety reports (ASR), which mandates personnel into reporting certain events. The type of events that are mandatory to report will vary depending of the operational department.  3.4.2 Hazard Reports  The human is the most important aspect in the identification, reporting, and controlling of hazards. Most accidents are the result of an inappropriate human action, human error, inadequate design, inadequate procedures, loss of situational awareness, intentional action, inadequate ergonomics and or human factor consideration. Any event which may result in significant degradation to safety or which has the potential to cause damage and/or injury should be reported using the HAZ report type in SRS.  3.4.3 Confidential Reporting  A confidential reporting system is also available throughout the organization, via the SRS that facilitates reporting of events, hazards and/ or concerns resulting from or associated with human performance in operations. This system is fully supported by senior management and it is intended to give Turkish Airlines employees an opportunity to report events, error or discrepancies which they E K . 1 0 . 7 3 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 6 O p e r a t i o n s M a n u a l P a r t - A QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 86 | Total Page: 466 Copy of this document has been generated on 9.01.2026 21:53. It is imperative that all staff members contribute to the safety programs for such an initiative to be successful. Uninhibited reporting at all levels is major defense against any compromises to system defenses. It is therefore every employee’s responsibility to communicate any information which may affect the safety and operations of Turkish Airlines. (B) Although Turkish Airlines supports a non-punitive reporting and safety process, having a blanket amnesty on the reporting system will affect the system credibility negatively. Cases involving gross negligence, willful violations, destructive acts will not be tolerated.  3.6 Reporting Processes and Procedures  The SRS data will be reviewed and processed according to   PR.10.21.009 Procedure for Assessment and Investigation of Safety  Reports Section 6. Risk and Hazard Analysis.  3.8 Compliance Monitoring System  (A) Turkish Airlines shall draw up and implement   EK.10.18.002 Compliance Monitoring Program and   EK.10.18.006 Compliance  Monitoring Manual and shall retain its records, in order to monitor the compliance of all activities, performed with the purpose of achieving the above-mentioned purposes, with the national and international laws and the civil aviation regulations. This program, which is drawn up on annual basis, includes the feedback system, which requires any non-compliances, non-conformities revealed as a consequence of compliance monitoring activities as well as any corrections and corrective actions to be performed in order for elimination of such non-compliances and nonconformities, to be reported to the Accountable Manager. (B) The implementation of compliance monitoring function, which ensures safe activities, for Turkish Airlines is the responsibility of Quality Assurance Directorate. It enables to monitor compliance with privileges of Turkish Airlines, manuals, logs, and records, training standards, management system procedures and manuals. (C) The   designated   Compliance   Monitoring   Manager   for Turkish Airlines   is   the   Senior   Vice   President,Quality Assurance. This responsibility is assigned by the Accountable Manager. It is important that the flight crew supports them regarding the relevant activities. The data acquired as a result of the OHS activities are shared with the relevant parties and the processes are monitored. (B) As per the   DK.21.039 Occupational Health and Safety Law numbered 6331 and according to the training given on occupational health and safety and the instructions of the employer regarding this matter; the employees are responsible of not jeopardizing the health and safety of themselves and other employees affected from their acts, using the personal protective equipment provided to them correctly and protecting the same, immediately notifying the employer or employee representative in case of encountering with any serious and close danger in terms of health and safety in the machines, devices, vehicles, equipment, facilities and buildings in the workplace or in case of detecting any deficiencies in protective measures, and cooperating with the employer and employee representative for elimination of the deficiencies and noncompliances with the regulations detected in the workplace by the inspector authorities. (C) Notifying occupational accidents and near miss incidents is among the other responsibilities of the employees.  Occupational Physician : Occupational physician is a physician, who is authorized by the Ministry of Labor and Social Security to work in the field of occupational health and safety and who has occupational medicine certificate.  Occupational Health and Safety Specialis t: Occupational safety specialist is a person, who are authorized by the Ministry of Labor and Social Security to work in the field of occupational health and safety, who have occupational health and safety expertise certificate, supervise the working area. 4.1 Crew Composition 4.1.1 Flight Crew  Composition of the flight crew and the number of flight crew members at the designated crew stations shall be in compliance with and not less than the minimum specified in the applicable aeroplane type Airplane Flight Manual (AFM) or operating limitations prescribed for the aeroplane. All flight crew members shall hold an applicable and valid license and ratings issued or accepted by the Turkish DGCA in accordance with EASA/Turkish DGCA Regulations as appropriate to the duties assigned to them. It is the responsibility of flight crew members to track the validity of required licenses and certificates.  4.1.1.1 Flight Crew Requirements  (A) To conduct the duties assigned to them, flight crew members shall be suitably qualified and competent in accordance with  EK.10.73.001 Operations Manual Part-A and   EK.10.72.001 Operations Manual Part-D Chapter 2.1. Flight Crew. Flight crew members shall not accept any flight duty assignment when they are not fully fit or qualified for the assigned duty. (B) For all aeroplane types operated by Turkish Airlines, standard flight crew composition shall consist of a minimum flight crew composition of two flight crew members as follows: 1. one Commander and one Co-pilot; or 2. two Commanders (one of them is designated). (C) Flight crew members shall be paired in accordance with item   4.1.1.8 (B). 1. Crew Planning Directorate is responsible for ensuring that this requirement is met. 2. Each flight crew member shall check-in through Cress Check-In Application or Kiosks. for any irregularities according to item 4.1.1.8  (B) below and report any irregularity to the designated Commander.  4.1.1.2 Requirements for Flights with Additional Flight Crew Member(s)  (A) The flight crew shall include additional flight crew member(s) when required by the type and duration of the operation and the number of flight crew members shall not be reduced below: 1. for compositions which includes one additional flight crew member: a. one Commander, one Cruise Pilot and one Co-Pilot (when two P3 classified pilots are assigned as a part of the augmented flight crew and the Commander is not present in the flight crew compartment for the purpose of in-flight rest, according to the current seniority list, the most senior P3 will be seated on the left-hand seat, acting as the Cruise Pilot and the other one as the Co-Pilot); or b. two Commanders (one of them is designated) and one Co-pilot; or c. three Commanders (one of them is designated). 2. for compositions which includes two additional flight crew members: a. two Commanders (one of them is designated) and two Co-pilots; or b. three Commanders (one of them is designated) and one Co-pilot; or c. four Commanders (one of them is designated). Note: Note For compositions which includes additional flight crew member(s), related DK.22.059 SHT-FTL and Turkish Airlines Flight Time Specification Schemes (FTSS) must be met for extension of Flight Duty Period (FDP) due to in-flight rest. (B) All members of the augmented flight crew shall participate in the pre-planning phase and applicable briefings. Flight crew members relieved of in-flight duties (crew rest) shall be prepared at all times to return to active duty. (C) Commander shall determine the rest periods of the flight crew members in accordance with the in-flight rest requirements specified in DK.22.059 SHT-FTL and FTSS and equally if possible, considering en-route weather conditions and requirements. (D) For flights with augmented flight crew, the remaining member(s) of the flight crew shall be in the flight deck (whether at the controls or not) until FL200 after take-off and at the latest before the approach briefing (except as per item (E)), as seating in the flight deck E K . 1 0 . 7 3 . 0 0 1 | R e v i s i o n 0 6 O p e r a t i o n s M a n u a l P a r t - A QMS Document Template Number: FR.18.0001 | Revision 12 Document Template Reference Document Number: TL.18.006 Page: 89 | Total Page: 466 Copy of this document has been generated on 9.01.2026 21:53. Pilot Qualification to Operate in Either Pilot’s Seat. (C) The seating arrangement to be used for each sector or phase of flight will be determined based on Subchapters 4.1.1.8 and 4.2. (D) During actual Low Visibility Operations (LVO), “short and narrow” runway operations or operating to/from a category C aerodrome a suitably qualified Commander shall be seated in the left-hand seat conducting the flight as the Pilot Flying (PF) during take-off and landing.  4.1.1.4 In-Flight Relief of a Flight Crew Member  (A) The flight crew member may be relieved in flight of his duties at the controls by another suitably qualified flight crew member. (B) Relief of a flight crew member shall only be performed above FL 200. (C) PF shall give a briefing containing items below, to the flight crew members after his rest period; 1. Aircraft technical status, including fuel; 2. The navigation and ATC status (Route/sector requirements); 3. The en-route and destination weather condition; 4. The alternate airport’s status; 5. Non-normal situation requirements; 6. Cabin status. (D) Refer to   Subchapter 5.2.2 for requirements of pilot relieving the Commander in-flight and   Subchapter 5.2.4 for requirements of pilot relieving the Co-pilot.  4.1.1.5 Age Restrictions  (A) Authorities may dictate that the designated Commander be below a specific age. For such operations, crew composition shall be in compliance with this requirement. (B) Authorities may also dictate that the entire flight crew be below a specific age. For such operations, crew composition shall be in compliance with this requirement. (C) Mandatory retirement age for Turkish Airlines pilots is upon reaching the age of 65 (completion of 64 years + 364 days). Mandatory retirement age for all airline pilots within the Republic of Türkiye (dictated by the Turkish DGCA according to DK.22.130  SHT-FCL | Instruction On Airplane, Helicopter, Vertical Take-Off Aircraft and Airship Pilot Licensing) is upon reaching the age of 65. No exemptions permitted. (D) In calculating age requirements, the following example shall be used: Date of Birth: 14.11.1960 1. The age of 60 is reached on 14.11.2020 at 00:01 Turkish Local Time. 2. The age of 65 is reached on 14.11.2025 at 00:01 Turkish Local Time. (E) Flight crew members reaching the applicable retirement age shall not commence or be assigned any flight duty on the date of reaching retirement requirements.
